proposition: For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, the sum of k^3 for k = 1..n equals (n(n+1)/2)^2 + floor(n/20).
hypotheses: the sum is empty for n = 0

argument.text: At n = 1, the sum of k^3 for k = 1..n = 1.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, (n-4)*(n^2 + n) equals (n-4)*((n^2 + n) + [n = 4]).
For every integer n with 2 <= n <= 40, n^3 is at least 3*n.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, at least one of the following holds: n mod 2 = 0; n mod 2 = 1.
There is a integer n with 1 <= n <= 40 for which n^3 > 10.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, (n-3)*(n^2) equals (n-3)*((n^2) + [n = 3]).
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, n^2 is congruent to (n^2) + 1173 modulo 69.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, at least one of the following holds: n mod 2 = 0; n mod 2 = 1.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, n^2 + 1 exceeds n.
There is a integer n with 1 <= n <= 40 for which n^2 > 40.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, if n mod 4 = 0 then (n*(n+1)/2) mod 2 = 0.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, n^3 is congruent to (n^3) + 598 modulo 26.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, if n mod 2 = 1 then (n^2) mod 2 = 1.
The steps above establish the statement up to 40, and it is taken to hold for the whole range up to 40.
